source.title: 拿比特币模型做 RSI，这思路太绝了！
source.source_status: Secondary technical report. The exact-title and project searches did not locate the original Kiki implementation or its source repository; platform scale and production claims are not independently established.
transferable_mechanisms: single-use task outputs and replay tombstones
root-level issuance counting and bounded ping-pong
deterministic acceptance rather than model self-report
Git and evidence-hash binding without claiming publisher authentication

design_correction.problem: Spending a root output to create children and also retaining that same root for later revocation would violate single-spend semantics.
design_correction.resolution: Mint creates one independent control ticket retained by the controller and one work ticket per planned job. Work transfers spend exactly one parent work ticket; revocation spends only the control ticket. Descendant liveness is derived from the control ticket.
design_correction.scope: No Bitcoin consensus, accounts, currency, signatures, blockchain, external settlement or autonomous RSI claim is introduced.

baseline_observation.interpretation: The legacy qfos-exec-v1 interface has no agent capability-ticket gate. This is a feature boundary, not by itself a claimed vulnerability.

criteria.pass: Minting binds the exact current wave plan, ledger hash, network and policy; it creates one control ticket plus one explicitly addressed work ticket per job, with deterministic validated identifiers. Duplicate job minting is rejected without mutation.

A missing ticket, wrong recipient, stale plan, forged ticket identifier, double spend or cross-root lineage mismatch fails closed and leaves both state and declared reports byte-for-byte unchanged or absent.

Only the current work-ticket recipient can transfer it. Transfer atomically spends the parent and creates one child for the exact same WaveJob and root. Root-wide sequence numbers are unique and contiguous.
The default root budget of twenty tickets is enforced across mint and every transfer branch. The attempt to create ticket twenty-one fails without spending its parent or creating a transaction.
Only the control-ticket recipient can revoke. Revocation spends the control ticket to no outputs and makes every descendant non-live; subsequent transfer or execution is rejected without mutation.

Authorized ticketed execution preserves qfos-exec-v1 outputs and commits execution outcomes, directive tombstones, ticket spends and the audit transaction in one staged LedgerSnapshot v5. Legacy execution and ticketed execution are reported separately.

A same-plan same-agent replay produces only skipped outcomes, creates no new ticket transaction and leaves the committed v5 state byte-for-byte unchanged. Spent tickets cannot be transferred or spent again.
Prompt-like text inside engine.sha256 payload remains data and produces an independently computable digest; it cannot replace the ticket-bound action or invoke shell/network/process execution.

An independent Python implementation reconstructs ticket and transaction identifiers, lineage, liveness, budgets and execution bindings from raw snapshots; known-answer self-tests and synthetic tamper rejection run before accepting the real report.

All pre-existing v4 fixtures and legacy execution controls remain byte-identical, the full gate passes from an implementation archive without .git and with an initially absent target, and the final differential uses that clean binary.

environment_corrections_before_implement: An initial placeholder registration timestamp was replaced with the measured system time before implementation; no result claim was attached to the placeholder.
The Rust toolchain was absent; stable, rustfmt and Clippy were installed through RsProxy before baseline construction. Toolchain installation is not counted as a security result.

A CARGO_TARGET_DIR under the non-executable /mnt/agents mount caused a build-script permission error before the old target ran. The baseline was rebuilt and executed under /tmp; only the successful run is recorded above.
